posts.title: The Numbers Going Into 2026-10-20
posts.author: Stan
posts.summary: No narrative here — just the model's current assessment of tonight's slate. Win probabilities are derived from our Elo-based ratings system, updated through yesterday's results. Projected margins follow from the same inputs. These aren't predictions in the crystal ball sense; they're probability distributions. A 65% win expectancy means the favorite wins roughly two out of every three times in that matchup scenario, not that they're guaranteed anything. The numbers reflect team strength as of this moment, filtered through home court adjustment and recent performance decay. Context—injuries, rest, rotation changes—lives outside the model until it shows up in actual results. What you're seeing below is the baseline: where the math stands before the ball goes up.

posts.title: The Numbers Going Into 2026-10-20
posts.author: Stan
posts.summary: No narrative here. No hot takes, no storylines about streaks or revenge games. Just the model's current read on the slate — win probabilities and projected margins derived from team ratings as they stand right now. These numbers reflect underlying strength, not who's riding momentum or playing with a chip on their shoulder. The probabilities are what they are because that's what the data supports given current form and matchup dynamics. If a team is favored by 8.7 points, that's the spread the model generates from its efficiency differentials and pace adjustments, not because 8.7 feels right or makes for a clean betting line. This is the baseline. Everything else is noise.
